name: cacio e pepe
instructions:
Cacio e pepe — the roman three-ingredient pasta: PECORINO ROMANO + BLACK PEPPER + PASTA WATER, emulsified into a sauce on the pasta. No butter, no oil, no cream in the classical build — the sauce is cheese + starch + water.

SERVES 2.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 8 oz (225g) spaghetti (or tonnarelli/bucatini)
- ~1 cup (100g) PECORINO ROMANO, finely grated (microplane or the smallest grater holes — fine matters for melting)
- 2 tsp whole black peppercorns, toasted and coarsely cracked (or ~1.5 tsp coarsely ground)
- salt (lightly — the pecorino is salty)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. TOAST THE PEPPER: crack the peppercorns and toast them in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, ~1 min. Set the skillet aside (the pasta finishes in it).
2. COOK THE PASTA in LESS WATER THAN USUAL (just enough to cover — you want the water starchy) with a light hand on the salt. Pull it 1-2 minutes shy of al dente. RESERVE AT LEAST A CUP OF PASTA WATER before draining.
3. MAKE THE CHEESE PASTE: while the pasta cooks, mash the grated pecorino with a few tablespoons of the hot pasta water in a bowl to form a thick, smooth paste. This pre-emulsification step is the main insurance against clumping.
4. MARRY: add the pasta to the skillet with the toasted pepper and a splash of pasta water over LOW heat; toss ~1 min to finish cooking and coat with pepper.
5. OFF THE HEAT, add the cheese paste and toss/stir vigorously, loosening with more pasta water a splash at a time, until the sauce is glossy and clings. TOO-HIGH HEAT IS THE FAILURE MODE — pecorino seizes into clumps above ~150°F; the residual heat of the pasta is enough.
6. Serve immediately with more pecorino and cracked pepper on top. The sauce tightens as it sits — it does not hold or reheat.

=== THE WHOLE DISH IS AN EMULSION PROBLEM ===

Cacio e pepe is three ingredients and one technique problem: getting pecorino to emulsify with starchy water instead of seizing into chewing-gum clumps. The standard insurance, in order of importance:
1. CHEESE PASTE FIRST — mash the finely-grated pecorino with hot pasta water into a paste before it ever meets the pasta.
2. OFF-HEAT MARRIAGE — the cheese goes in off the flame; pecorino seizes when overheated.
3. STARCHY WATER — cook the pasta in less water than usual so the reserved water carries enough starch to stabilize the emulsion.
4. FINE GRATE — coarse shreds melt unevenly and clump before they disperse.

=== PECORINO ROMANO, NOT PARMESAN ===

Pecorino romano (sheep's milk, saltier, sharper) is the canonical cheese — it IS the 'cacio.' Parmesan melts more forgivingly and some recipes cut the pecorino with it as training wheels, but it reads sweeter/nuttier and the dish drifts away from its roman identity.

=== PEPPER IS A CO-LEAD, NOT A SEASONING ===

The pepper is toasted and present in quantity — it's the second headliner, not a finishing grind. Toasting whole peppercorns and cracking them coarsely is the standard move for aroma plus bite.
